_comment: Day-one Discord structure + project template. Consumed by Phase 2/3 automation: find-or-create by exact name, safe to re-apply anytime (idempotent). Rules & per-instance setup: docs/DISCORD.md

channels.name: omnius
channels.purpose: main door - talk to Omnius; any message wakes/spawns it on demand. Named for the persona; the category is 🎛 ORCHESTRATOR.

channels.name: daybook
channels.topic: quick capture -> daybook: notes, tasks, voice notes (transcribed)
channels.purpose: personal capture; its OWN desk so note-taking never occupies the orchestrator. Notes are stored, questions are answered.

channels.name: fleet-status
channels.topic: bot-maintained fleet overview - pinned embed, do not post
channels.purpose: read-only dashboard, updated by /status and every fleet mutation

channels.name: transcribe
channels.topic: send a recording (or its path) -> transcript, frames, notes
channels.purpose: the recordings desk: meetings, calls, videos, audio. Its OWN desk because a 2h job takes ~25 min and reading the transcript back costs ~40k tokens - neither may occupy the orchestrator. It starts a DETACHED job and returns at once.

channels.name: alerts
channels.topic: errors and approval requests from all sessions
channels.purpose: attention needed; Phase 4: Approve/Deny buttons for destructive ops

categories.name: 📧 EMAIL
categories._why_session_on_the_category: Every channel here maps to ONE desk. build_map reads this instead of needing a branch per account, and the envelope carries channelId so a reply lands back in the right account's channel.
categories._why_channelsFrom: Channels are per ACCOUNT, and accounts are added by editing config/email.ini - not by editing this file. ensure_structure() stamps one channel per [account.<label>] at watchdog startup, so adding an account is the only step. nameFrom=user names the channel after the ADDRESS (someone@example.com -> #someone-example) because a label like 'gmail' stops meaning anything the moment there are two of them - his question, 2026-08-06.
